q: We live in a small apartment with thin walls in Korea. Our neighbour is very vocal when she’s annoyed by noise, so I’m afraid of prolonged crying. To handle the worst of the crying and teach him to settle himself, we booked a hotel room near our apartment.
cx: Mother of an almost-11-month-old nursed to sleep after jet lag; five nights in a hotel to sleep train.

q: Now, nursing is my only tool, and he demands to be nursed back to sleep every time he wakes up. […] Tonight, I decided to stop nursing him because I’m exhausted of being trapped into nursing for long hours.
cx: Baby who always self-settled now needs nursing at every waking.

q: 2.5 hours later, he woke up crying. My husband supported him, and he cried for almost 1.5 hours before falling asleep.
cx: First night of training in the hotel room.

q: So does this mean that I just continue to do things in survival mode meaning nursing since it’s the only method that works right now?
cx: Reply after a commenter says to fix jet lag first.

q: Currently mine start crying as soon as I put them in their crib and I’m just afraid how hard it will be to hear him cry 4x now instead of only once.
cx: Week one of Ferber at night for a 7-month-old; dreading nap training.

q: Kinda nervous to drop to 2 naps but this is the advice I see the most ❤️
cx: Following the most common subreddit advice.

q: For the past 10 months, I’ve had zero issues putting my baby boy to sleep. […] Now, as soon as I pick him up for bedtime, he starts crying and squirming like crazy. The second I hand him over to my wife, he calms down almost instantly.

q: Could taking a 3-day break cause this big of a sudden preference for Mom, or is this just a classic separation anxiety phase?
cx: Father missed three bedtimes with back pain (and got a haircut).

q: She’s getting about 11 hours on average according to Huckleberry and I can’t see how to improve it.
cx: UK parent of a 5-week-old who only naps on a parent's chest, measuring against the recommended 14-17 hours.

q: I don’t want to go full blackout because I want her to be able to sleep in daylight (as she eventually will in nursery) but is that the only way?
cx: Same parent.

q: Our 2 yrs old daughter has never been a great sleeper, but we’re at the point where my wife and I are completely exhausted and really need to figure out how to fix this.
cx: Father of a 2-year-old rocked to sleep, waking 3-5 times a night; sleep trained at 7 months then regressed.

q: She can sleep herself IN DAYCARE AND AT GRANDPARENTS HOME BUT JUST NOT AT HOME.
cx: Same father.

q: She used to sleep in a crib, but she started climbing out, so she's now in a toddler bed. That makes CIO much harder because she can simply get out of bed. Looking back, we really wish we had worked harder on independent sleep while she was still in the crib
cx: Same father.

q: Eventually we get so tired that we give in and rock her to sleep again. […] We don't want to keep changing strategies every few nights and confusing her even more.
cx: Same father asking what actually worked for others.

q: She still wakes up 3-10x a night and needs either a hand placed on her or something more (I always start with least intervention possible). I am the only one able to put her to sleep and soothe her if she wakes up.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of an 18-month-old sleeps on a floor bed next to the toddler's bed.

q: **She has not been sleep trained (and can't be for medical reasons... please do not recommend this**) so to survive I sleep on a floor bed next to her toddler bed.
cx: Same mother ruling out the usual reply up front.

q: Bonus points if one day she can sleep peacefully knowing that I will return for her if she truly needs something and eventually be able to be put down for a nap/bed by another trusted individual (my husband or one of her 4 incredibly gushing grandparents).
cx: Same mother on her goal.

q: My back is in constant pain now from how much time she has spent in a carrier or on my hip (literally countless hours) over the course of her life
cx: Same mother on her body.

q: We have had to Co-sleep because he has terrible Silent Reflux that I've been to countless doctors to no avail.
cx: Mother of a 9-month-old who sleeps well only in the parents' bed.

q: Co-sleeping has been great and I do love the closeness and waking up to his face every morning but I would like our bed back.
cx: Same mother.

q: he is such an alert and attached baby (also very determined) that I feel that all the traditional sleep training methods are not an option. Maybe I'll wait until he's a toddler where he has some more understanding to try again. I have no idea.

q: I've tried just putting him in and walking out the room, he panics and cries so hard that he chokes. I'm not going to leave him like that it's no fun for either of us
cx: Reply to a commenter suggesting she leave the room.

q: I can never get my 3yo to stay contained in another room or be quiet if im trying to get my 5mo down for a nap in the same room. […] I tried keeping her in another room but she always comes to where I am and ruins the nap.

q:

What we've tried more specifically: moving bedtime later, more food, more activities, less activities, making naps longer, capping naps, extending the first two ww by 15 minutes.

q: Everyone around me has babies that sleep though the night or only has one wakeup and that is without sleep training. I don't know what I'm doing wrong.
